mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to monetary tightening, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% and 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises > 0.5% in 1 month and 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) for two consecutive months signals a weakening consumer demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS declines for 2 consecutive months and 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases > 1% in 1 month and 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 45% of instances, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% signals an accommodative monetary policy, which typically boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS < 1% and 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline and unemployment (UNRATE) rises simultaneously, it signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST declines and UNRATE rises simultaneously, and 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances, or if Rank IC for this interaction remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payroll employment (PAYEMS) for three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which typically boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases for 3 consecutive months and 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 45% of instances, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, reflecting the market's positive response to accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS < 2% and 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances, or if Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.
